page: Vultr vx1-g-32c-128g-1920s is a general-purpose server from the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor with 16 physical cores and 2 threads per core, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. Storage is bundled with a 1920 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark results show strong performance characteristics across multiple domains. Single-core CPU performance via stress-ng is in the top tier, while multi-core performance is in the average tier. Memory performance is notable, with large-block write bandwidth ranking in the top tier and large-block read bandwidth in the strong tier. The processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and cryptography standards like AES and SHA_NI, contributing to strong Passmark CPU extended instructions and encryption test scores.

Given its balanced vCPU-to-RAM ratio and high-speed local NVMe storage, this server is well-suited for database operations, static web serving, and data compression tasks. It demonstrates strong performance in Redis SET operations and Passmark database tests. Additionally, CPU-based LLM inference tasks perform well, with small model text generation reaching top-tier speeds and large model generation achieving strong results. The dedicated AMD EPYC cores and bundled NVMe storage offer a resource-dense profile, delivering high qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring consistent CPU performance and fast local storage without the overhead of GPU accelerators.
